newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds decide to bid at CVRD auction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds decide to bid at CVRD auction.

text.p: A group of pension funds has decided to join one of the consortiums bidding at the April 29 privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD , a pension fund spokesman said.

"The pension funds have decided to bid at the auction, but no accord has been signed yet with any of the consortia participating in the auction," said a spokesman for the Banco do Brasil pension fund Previ, Brazil's largest.

Under the privatization rules, the pension funds had to decide today whether as minority CVRD shareholders they would sell their stake at the auction alongside the government's CVRD shares or whether they would join a consortium to bid in the sell-off.
If the pension funds had decided to sell their joint 15-percent stake at the auction then the CVRD sell-off would have become unviable due to the privatization rules and would have been postponed.

The rules stipulate that the government has to sell off at least 40 percent of CVRD voting shares but that the total stake on sale April 29 cannot exceed 45 percent, which would have been the case if the pension funds sold their stake as well.
The pension funds have been coveted by both the consortia taking part in the auction because of their existing stake in CVRD.
The new owners of the 40-45 percent share block will have a controling position in CVRD if the pension funds are on its side.

Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp today formalized their partnership in a consortium called Valecom which is likely to also include a group of 12 Japanese companies led by Nippon Steel and Banco Safra.

Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN is leading the second consortium likely to include pulp and paper firm Cia. Suzano, construction firm Camargo Correia, metal and metallurgical company Caemi, Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management and South Africa's Gencor.
